dedupe_keys.name: texas february 2021 blackout open source extendable synthetic grid model and assessment of corrective measures

description: This study releases an open-source, extendable synthetic model of the Texas power grid, with open cross-domain data sets, and uses it to assess measures that could have eased the February 2021 blackout, when winter storms caused at least 69 deaths and 4.5 million customer interruptions through wide generation outages and record demand. Dongqi Wu, Xiangtian Zheng, Chanan Singh and Le Xie of Texas A&M University and Yixing Xu, Daniel Olsen and Bainan Xia of Breakthrough Energy Sciences published it in Advances in Applied Energy in November 2021. The model is synthetic but calibrated to published data, and simulation captures the main features of the event; the authors test corrective measures, including generator winterization, quantify their effect on severity, and show regional disparities in load shedding. Coverage is the Texas interconnection. Format and access: open access article describing the released model and data; the repository link was not seen in the part of the page read. Licence: Creative Commons article licence, variant not read; free. Caveats: a synthetic network only approximates the real one, and outage inputs are reconstructed from public reports. It supports network flow, resilience and cascading failure studies of cold-weather grid failures. Related catalogue records are the Texas February 2021 blackout case and the Texas A&M synthetic grid test cases.
